surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Devils take down the Ducks
paras: Arseny Gritsyuk struck first for the Devils early in the first, his fourth straight game with a goal. Nico Hischier made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period. Tim Washe cut New Jersey’s lead to 2-1 midway through the third, but they got no closer. Anthony Mantha stretched the lead to 3-1 late in the period, and Jack Hughes added an empty-net goal with just 7 seconds left to make it 4-1.

The Devils carried the play, outshooting the Ducks 29-17, and got the result to match. Nico Daws made 16 saves for the Devils, and Ville Husso stopped 25 of 28. The Devils moved to 6-4-0, and the Ducks dropped to 4-6-0.

items.text: Jack Hughes passed Pat Verbeek for ninth on the Devils’ all-time goals list, with 171.
The Ducks are on a five-game losing streak.
Jeff Malott and Pavel Mintyukov were in NHL.com’s projected lineup but didn’t dress.
Two of the preview’s four calls held.
